clue.text: Nick involves Penny in firm's dance

indicators.note: the penny is put in the middle of the firm's dance, splitting it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm, and the 's adds S
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A police raid nabs a cheap coin at a company party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for a police station, so it is the definition here, not a verb meaning steal or arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang both words name a police station.

clue.text: Writer's problem concerning climbing aid?

parts.note: writer's cramp is a painful hand condition
on means concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: An author's hand ache relates to some mountaineering gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is a spiked plate fixed to a boot to help on ice when climbing.

clue.text: Miner crossing lake over hill is an old fraud!

indicators.note: the hill goes over into the middle of the word
the miner word lies across the lake, holding it

parts.note: a pitman is a coal miner
a down is a rolling chalk hill in southern England

explanation.surface: A coal miner's trek across water and hills is exposed as a hoax.
explanation.walkthrough: Piltdown Man was a fake early human skull 'found' in Sussex in 1912 and exposed in 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed fossil human was a notorious forgery, so it is a fraud from long ago.

clue.text: Compassionate article framed by Scottish philosopher

indicators.note: the article sits inside the philosopher's name like a picture in a frame

parts.note: David Hume was an 18th-century Scottish philosopher
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A kindly piece of writing hangs within a frame bearing a thinker's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means showing compassion and kindness.

clue.text: Expressionless person prodding brave duke?

parts.note: someone who prods is a poker
to brave a danger is to face it

explanation.surface: Someone jabs a courageous nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective describing the duke; it is the verb face.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker player hides feelings, so the compound means showing no expression.

clue.text: Violating rule, beginning to parody City jargon

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here of parody

parts.note: EC is the postal district code for the City of London
cant is the special jargon of a group

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a rule by mocking the language of financiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Peccant means sinning or offending, that is, breaking a rule of conduct.

clue.text: Security man on board

definitions.meaning: something left as a pledge against a loan

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an item pledged as security and the humblest chessman on the board.

clue.text: Ill-humoured lover reportedly given weapon

parts.note: cross means bad-tempered

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so a homophone follows

parts.note: a beau is a lover or boyfriend

explanation.surface: A sulky boyfriend is handed a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbow is a mechanical bow firing bolts, a weapon.

clue.text: Snake bites head off insect

indicators.note: the head of the insect word, its first letter, is cut off

parts.note: a wasp is an insect

explanation.surface: A serpent decapitates a bug with a bite.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a venomous snake, famous for killing Cleopatra.

clue.text: For 'that reason part of the army's in reserve

parts.note: taken as written
RE, the Royal Engineers, is the army corps that 'part of' points to; 's is a link
by means aside or in reserve, as in putting money by

explanation.surface: Explaining why a unit is held back from action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' tells you to take one unit of the army, the Royal Engineers, rather than the whole army.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby means by that means, as a result of that.

clue.text: Reportedly the totality of leather-workers use it

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so a homophone is wanted

parts.note: the totality of something is all of it

explanation.surface: Rumour has it every leather craftsman uses this tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed tool for piercing holes is standard kit for workers in leather.

clue.text: Let one's hair down and force tiny ring into it

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them

indicators.note: the ring is pushed into the tiny word, which 'it' points back to

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: An instruction to relax while jamming a little ring somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the tiny word, so 'into' puts the ring inside that word rather than inside something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for having fun without restraint, celebrating wildly.

clue.text: Favourite lines about Chaucer's hair-splitting?

indicators.note: pet goes about, around, the next piece

parts.note: a favourite is a pet
Dan, meaning master, is the title Chaucer gives people, as in Dan Chaucer's own era
RY, railway, is crossword shorthand for lines

explanation.surface: A scholar's beloved verses about Chaucer turn into quibbling over trifles.
explanation.walkthrough: DAN is an archaic title meaning master or sir, found in Chaucer and Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive fuss over fine detail, exactly what hair-splitting describes.

clue.text: Posh fur at one's disposal

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech
sable is a costly fur

explanation.surface: An upmarket fur coat is there for you to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available for use is at one's disposal.

clue.text: Put up with humour before Head appears to testify

parts.note: to bear something is to put up with it
wit is humour
a ness is a headland, a promontory

explanation.surface: Tolerating jokes before the boss arrives to give evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a headmaster or boss; it is a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness is to give testimony, to testify.

clue.text: Inert males difficult to make more efficient

indicators.note: the letters are made hard to read, hence rearranged

explanation.surface: Lazy men are hard to make more productive.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline an organisation is to simplify it so it works more efficiently.

clue.text: All the main points of the bulletin

definitions.meaning: the four main points of the compass, North, East, West and South, written by their initials

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the compass points as letters, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a broadcast report of current events, and the compass initials together spell the word.

clue.text: Serving to warn amusing person always crossing river

parts.note: a caution is an informal word for an amusing or remarkable person

indicators.note: the always word stretches across the river, holding it

parts.note: ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A comic who keeps fording a river is meant as a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Cautionary means giving a warning, as in a cautionary tale.

clue.text: Poet without energy — an emaciated type

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the poet goes outside the energy

parts.note: John Skelton was a Tudor poet
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A poet lacking vigour is a gaunt figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like minus; here it means outside, so SKELTON wraps E.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin person is called a skeleton, an informal hyperbole.

clue.text: Athletics' official has porridge with museum employee

parts.note: porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, which is also called time
a keeper is a curator in a museum

explanation.surface: A track judge eats oats alongside a curator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' wants to be breakfast; it is British slang for time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who records times in races is the official in athletics who keeps the clock.

clue.text: Bill, a northerner, wasting time in Mexican state

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

indicators.note: the northerner wastes, loses, the time

parts.note: a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A Scotsman squanders time paying a tab in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a state in south-east Mexico, which gave its name to the sauce.

clue.text: Suddenly catch on and shoot

definitions.meaning: a small slender shoot of a tree or plant

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British informal for realising suddenly, and also a small branch, a plant's shoot.

clue.text: Gallery gets wind up? What a stroke of luck

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
to wind up is to end

explanation.surface: A gallery closing down turns out to be a stroke of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gallery' suggests an art gallery; the gods is the cheap top balcony of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected piece of good fortune, which the exclamation expresses.

clue.text: Like the licence given to linesmen?

definitions.text: Like the licence given to linesmen?

parts.words: Like the licence given to linesmen?
parts.note: linesmen are read as writers of lines of verse, whose freedom with rules is a famous kind of licence

explanation.definitionFit: Writers of verse are granted freedom with grammar and fact, the licence of their art.

clue.text: British crook displaying charm perhaps.

parts.note: a crook is a bend, as is an angle

explanation.surface: A British criminal is shown off as a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a criminal; it is a bend, an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm and a rigid bracelet are both items of jewellery, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Brought in from island refuge surrounded by sea

indicators.note: the refuge sits with the sea all round it

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
a port is a haven or refuge

explanation.surface: Goods arrive from an island harbour ringed by water.
explanation.definitionFit: Imported goods are ones brought in from abroad.

clue.text: Stop TV doctor going over area

indicators.note: in a down clue the doctor sits over, above, the area

parts.note: Doctor Who is a long-running BBC television series

explanation.surface: A television physician pauses to cover a region.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a call to a horse to stop.

clue.text: Summary treatment produces resistance in abrupt workers

parts.note: an abrupt reply is a short one

indicators.note: resistance is placed in the workers word

parts.note: a shift is a group of workers on duty together
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Curt staff respond to opposition by dealing with it quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Short shrift is brusque, perfunctory treatment, a summary dismissal.

clue.text: Character said to be in debt

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so a word heard alike is wanted

parts.note: a character is a letter, here O

explanation.surface: A person admits they owe money.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe is to be indebted to someone.

clue.text: Storm centre? Yes, sounds like it

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: aye means yes

explanation.surface: Someone affirms that a storm's calm middle is what is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The calm middle of a hurricane is called its eye.

clue.text: One taking a canoe trip around Pacific islands

indicators.note: the letters go tripping around into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller paddles a canoe around the South Seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' joins I to A CANOE; together those seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the name for the region of Pacific island groups including Australasia.

clue.text: Made allowances for former copper's little boy

parts.note: ex means former
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and the 's adds S
Ed is a short name for a boy, Edward

explanation.surface: A retired policeman's young son is let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is the metal, symbol Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone is to forgive or make allowances for them.
